question: What is the ratio of the volume of a cone to that of a cylinder having the same base radius and height?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For identical base radius (r) and height (h):

Volume of a Cone = 1/3 × Base Area × Height

Volume of a Cylinder = 1 × Base Area × Height

Ratio (Cone : Cylinder) = (1/3) : 1 = 1 : 3

**∴ Answer = 1:3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of cone = Radius of cylinder = r

Height of cone = Height of cylinder = h

**Formula used:**

Volume of Cone (V₁) = (1/3)πr²h

Volume of Cylinder (V₂) = πr²h

**Calculations:**

Ratio = Volume of Cone : Volume of Cylinder

⇒ Ratio = [(1/3) × π × r² × h] : [π × r² × h]

⇒ Dividing both sides by (π × r² × h):

⇒ Ratio = (1/3) : 1

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1:3 (Option 3).**</p
